description.narrative: The development objectives of the project are to improve the condition of the national paved road network, to lower transport cost on selected roads, and to expand the capacity of selected regional airports.

The objective of the Transport Sector Support Project for Tanzania are to improve the condition of the national paved road network, to lower transport cost on selected roads, and to expand the capacity of selected regional airports. There are five components to the project, the first component being rehabilitation and preparation of designs for the rehabilitation of paved trunk roads. The second component is the improvement of regional airports. This component will be implemented by the Tanzanian Airports Authority (TAA). Under this component the paving and rehabilitation of the runway at Kigoma airport, the rehabilitation of the main runway at Tabora airport, as well as the extension, rehabilitation, and resurfacing of the runway at Bukoba airport, with the replacement of the current apron, terminal, car parking, and other facilities, will be financed. The third component is the improvement of road safety. This component will be implemented by Ministry of Infrastructure Development (MoID). It will support the establishment of the National Road Safety Agency (NRSA), the Driver and Vehicle Examination and Licensing Agency (DVELA), and the development of a Road Accident Information System (RAIS), as proposed in the recently adopted National Road Safety Policy (NRSP). The fourth component is the promotion of public-private partnerships; (ii) feasibility studies of potential Public-Private Partnership (PPP) projects; and (iii) transaction advisors for projects that were found feasible. Finally, the fifth component is the emergency road and bridge repair.
